title: Best-of-N session boundaries
summary: A best-of-N session MUST run N candidate runs in isolated worktrees under harness-owned lifecycle commands, MUST leave candidate repair and exclusion to the operator, and MUST NOT perform any source-control action.
instructions: The projected `pan-meta-orchestrator` agent MUST be the only start surface for a best-of-N session.
The meta-orchestrator MUST run as a nested subagent and directly perform supervisor mechanics for every session child run.
The meta-orchestrator MUST NOT delegate a child run to another `pan-orchestrator`, because a second-level supervisor cannot launch workers.
The meta-orchestrator MUST delegate stages to run-scoped worker agents with foreground, blocking calls.
One prepared invocation MUST have at most one active worker at a time.
After an interruption, a resumed session MUST reconcile session and candidate state through harness status commands before further delegation.
Before a relaunch on the same invocation, the supervisor MUST confirm the prior worker ended, following the referenced supervisor-recovery guidance.
Evidence of concurrent workers in one candidate worktree MUST stop that candidate's delegation and MUST be surfaced to the operator with the run id, invocation id, and overlap evidence.
The session lifecycle MUST run through `./bin/pan best-of-n` commands. Agents MUST NOT create worktrees, candidate runs, run-scoped agent variants, or session records by hand.
Every candidate run MUST execute in its own detached worktree under `runtime/worktrees/<bon-id>/`, and MUST NOT edit the main workspace.

Candidate runs MUST use the gates their workflow declares. A best-of-N session MUST NOT add an operator stop to a candidate run, and MUST NOT relax the operator gate the consolidation run declares for release preparation.
A terminal candidate failure MUST remain session evidence and MUST NOT create an operator gate.
The meta-orchestrator MUST stop only when a non-terminal candidate cannot execute because required bytes, state, workspace, authentication, or tools are unavailable.
Exclusion of a candidate MUST come from an explicit operator directive and MUST be recorded with `./bin/pan best-of-n abandon`.
Consolidation MUST start only when every candidate run is terminal or recorded as abandoned, and at least one candidate succeeded. A session with no successful candidate MUST be reported as blocked.
The consolidation request MUST name every candidate, including an abandoned one, with its run id, worktree path, final status, and output paths.
A best-of-N session MUST NOT create a commit, push, merge, branch deletion, or history rewrite, in the main workspace or in any worktree.
Worktree removal is destructive and operator-owned. `./bin/pan best-of-n clean` MUST refuse a dirty worktree without an explicit force flag, and MUST NOT delete a branch or a commit.
Global best-of-N pruning MUST always skip active sessions. It MUST skip dirty worktrees unless the operator supplies `--force`.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you resume an interrupted session or relaunch a worker on a prepared invocation.
